result.title: Can Large Language Model Agents Learn by Watching Tutorial Videos?
result.summary: Humans continuously acquire knowledge from carefully crafted materials such as books and tutorial videos, carrying that understanding into future tasks. Millions of such instructional videos are uploaded online every day, yet LLM agents remain unable to exploit this ever-expanding wealth of human teaching. Their capabilities are frozen after training, while parameter updates at scale remain prohibitively expensive. This raises the central question: can LLM agents learn from this vast instructional resource without parameter updates? We introduce Tutorial Agentic Learning (TAL), a nonparametric continual-learning paradigm that consolidates tutorial videos into a persistent, structured tutorialbook memory through a two-stage adversarial process that harvests hard, video-grounded questions and uses them to refine the memory. At inference time, TAL retrieves through a Table-of-Contents (TOC) tree, tying retrieval directly to the model's reasoning rather than to embedding similarity. To study this setting, we introduce VidLearn, a multimodal QA benchmark built from 72 chess tutorial videos spanning 12 openings. On VidLearn, TAL outperforms all evaluated baselines and improves monotonically as more videos are consumed, achieving up to 113% and 91% relative gains over the corresponding vanilla MLLMs on the training and test splits, respectively. In actual gameplay, TAL reaches a stronger opening-phase position than its vanilla counterpart in 69% of head-to-head games. Evaluation in a second domain further demonstrates the generality of TAL. Together, these results highlight instructional videos as a scalable resource for parameter-update-free agent continual learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TAL：一种无需参数更新的持续学习范式，把教学视频整理为结构化的 tutorialbook 记忆，并通过两阶段对抗式流程挖掘视频接地的难题来精炼该记忆；同时构建基于 72 个国际象棋教程视频的 VidLearn 基准进行评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 用 TOC 树把检索与推理过程绑定、再以难题筛选精炼外部记忆的做法，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选与训练监督提供线索；但其机制依赖非参数化外部记忆而非 latent 状态，迁移可行性有待核查。
